title: Zebra: Efficient Redundant Array of Zoned Namespace SSDs Enabled by Zone Random Write Area (ZRWA)
problem: Integrating ZNS SSDs into RAID configurations requires handling partial parity updates (PPUs) that arise from ZNS's append-only write semantics; existing metadata-zone-based solutions become performance bottlenecks under high PPU workloads.
motivation: ZNS SSDs reduce device-level garbage collection overhead and enable predictable storage performance, but RAID configurations over ZNS SSDs are severely limited by the latency of dedicated metadata zones required to manage PPUs.
method: Zebra exploits the Zone Random Write Area (ZRWA), the SSD's internal write buffer in front of each zone, to handle PPUs in-place. By ensuring that parity chunks fit within the ZRWA window, Zebra performs partial parity overrides within the buffer rather than writing to separate metadata zones. A set of complementary techniques maintain high performance and reliability across both large-zone and small-zone ZNS SSD models.
key_novelty: Using the ZRWA (the SSD's native write buffer window) as the target storage for parity partial updates in ZNS RAID, matching the repeated sequential overwrite I/O pattern of PPUs to the ZRWA's random-write capability.
contributions: Zebra architecture that maps ZNS RAID parity partial updates to the ZRWA write buffer
Analysis identifying repeated sequential overwrite as the dominant PPU I/O pattern
Techniques ensuring both high performance and data reliability under diverse ZNS RAID workloads
1.1x to 4.2x throughput improvement over RAIZN on micro and application benchmarks

metrics.speedup: 1.1x to 4.2x throughput improvement vs RAIZN ZNS RAID system

limitations: Evaluation is limited to two ZNS SSD models; ZRWA window size constraints may limit applicability to workloads with large parity chunks.
primary_theme: ZNS RAID partial parity management via ZRWA exploitation
